issues.description: signing_mode_enum relies on an implicit fall-through instead of an explicit four-branch truth table.
issues.detail: Three explicit elif branches followed by a bare 'return CHIP_0002' silently handles the (not is_hex, safe_mode) case. The postcondition holds only by accident of branch order. Spell out all four combinations with a match or explicit final branch so the next reader (and the next CHIP mode) does not have to reconstruct the truth table.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring still references a stale 'request' parameter that no longer exists.
issues.detail: The extracted function now takes (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address) as keyword args, but the docstring is a copy-paste artifact reading ':param request:'. Stale docs on a freshly extracted library function are worse than no docs — either describe the new parameters or remove the stub.

issues.description: Mode-to-bytes dispatch is duplicated between sign_message and verify_signature.
issues.detail: The same SigningMode -> bytes mapping is encoded in both functions in the new util module, and the two disagree on whether unknown modes raise or silently default to CHIP_0002. Extract a single _message_to_bytes(mode, message) helper with one consistent totality discipline so the next CHIP mode cannot be added in one place and forgotten in the other.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is misplaced on the base Wallet and reached via main_wallet for unrelated DID/NFT keys.
issues.detail: The transformation is a pure synthetic-key derivation with no instance state and nothing to do with main_wallet identity. RPC callers reach through wallet_state_manager.main_wallet to derive keys for DID/NFT wallets. Move it to chia/wallet/util/signing.py as a free function (or at minimum a staticmethod) to fix the boundary.

issues.description: util/signing.py leaks the RPC response type VerifySignatureResponse into the utility layer.
issues.detail: The signing utility imports and returns VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types. Its contract should be (mode, key, message, signature[, address]) -> bool plus an error reason, not an RPC-shaped DTO. The coupling means the util cannot be reused without dragging the RPC schema along and ties it to request-types evolution.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address never asserts the verify result.
issues.detail: The test awaits verify_signature and discards the return value. The postcondition under test is 'verify returns isValid=True', but the test would pass even if verify returned VerifySignatureResponse(isValid=False). Add the explicit assertion on the returned isValid field.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a well-motivated mechanical extraction of sign_message and verify_signature into chia/wallet/util/signing.py, moving toward a single source of truth for message signing. However, the extraction stops one step short of its own goal: mode-to-bytes dispatch is still duplicated between sign and verify, signing_mode_enum relies on a fall-through default rather than an explicit truth table, and sign/verify disagree on how to treat unknown modes. Boundary issues remain — convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is misplaced on Wallet, and the util module leaks the RPC response type. A stale docstring and a missing test assertion round out the cleanup. Small, fixable, then land.
